post_topic: LLM-agnostic architecture vs. vendor lock-in: why enterprises are buying the wrong thing
scene_description: A split architectural diagram showing three vendor-specific AI platforms — Azure OpenAI, Bedrock, and Vertex — feeding into a single provider-agnostic orchestration layer labeled with config-driven routing, audit logging, and HITL escalation triggers, with a local Ollama instance branching off for air-gapped environments. Below the abstraction layer, calling code sits unchanged while above it the vendor boxes are interchangeable, visually emphasizing the decoupling. The tension is between vendor lock-in (deep SDK coupling on one side) and LLM-agnostic infrastructure (the unified routing table on the other), set against a technical blueprint-style background referencing the Cloud Decoded system.
